course.title: AP U.S. History
course.description: Trace how Americans have argued over identity, power, work, and their place in the world, from the societies that existed before 1491 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Follow the nation's development from early contact and colonization through independence, civil war, industrialization, world wars, and recent decades.

unit.title: Period 3
unit.description: Follow the Seven Years' War, the road to independence, the Revolution, the Articles of Confederation and the Constitution, and the first political parties from 1754 to 1800.

firstTopic.title: Contextualizing Period 3
firstTopic.summary: How the Seven Years' War, British imperial reform, colonial self-government, and Enlightenment ideas set the stage for independence and the first experiments in republican government, 1754–1800.

topic.title: The Seven Years’ War (The French and Indian War)
topic.summary: Why Britain and France went to war over the North American interior, how Britain won, and how victory left Britain in debt and set the stage for new imperial policies and colonial resentment.

framework.name: Course themes
framework.title: Use the course themes to choose your evidence
framework.intro: The themes connect developments across all nine periods. A piece of evidence can fit more than one theme; choose the one that answers the prompt.
framework.sourceNote: Theme names, codes, and descriptions follow the AP U.S. History Course and Exam Description (fall 2026).

themes.title: American and National Identity
themes.description: This theme focuses on how and why definitions of American and national identity and values have developed among the diverse and changing population of North America as well as on related topics, such as citizenship, constitutionalism, foreign policy, assimilation, and American exceptionalism.
themes.question: Who counted as American, and what did people believe the nation stood for?
themes.example: Debates over ratifying the Constitution turned on what kind of republic Americans wanted.

themes.title: Work, Exchange, and Technology
themes.description: This theme focuses on the factors behind the development of systems of economic exchange, particularly the role of technology, economic markets, and government.
themes.question: How did people earn a living, trade, and use new technology?
themes.example: Canals and railroads tied farmers in the West to markets in the East.

themes.title: Geography and the Environment
themes.description: This theme focuses on the role of geography and both the natural and human-made environments in the social and political developments in what would become the United States.
themes.question: How did land, climate, and resources shape choices, and how did people change them?
themes.example: The Chesapeake's climate suited tobacco, which shaped its labor system.

themes.title: Migration and Settlement
themes.description: This theme focuses on why and how the various people who moved to and within the United States both adapted to and transformed their new social and physical environments.
themes.question: Why did people move, and how did they change the places they settled?
themes.example: The Great Migration brought African Americans from the rural South to northern cities.

themes.title: Politics and Power
themes.description: This theme focuses on how different social and political groups have influenced society and government in the United States as well as how political beliefs and institutions have changed over time.
themes.question: Who held power, how did they use it, and who challenged it?
themes.example: The New Deal expanded the federal government's role in the economy.

themes.title: America in the World
themes.description: This theme focuses on the interactions between nations that affected North American history in the colonial period and on the influence of the United States on world affairs.
themes.question: How did contact, trade, diplomacy, and war connect America to other nations?
themes.example: The Seven Years' War left Britain in debt and changed its policies toward the colonies.

themes.title: American and Regional Culture
themes.description: This theme focuses on the how and why national, regional, and group cultures developed and changed as well as how culture has shaped government policy and the economy.
themes.question: How did beliefs, religion, arts, and media develop and shape public life?
themes.example: The Second Great Awakening inspired many Americans to join reform movements.

themes.title: Social Structures
themes.description: This theme focuses on how and why systems of social organization develop and change as well as the impact that these systems have on the broader society.
themes.question: How were people ranked by race, class, and gender, and how did that change?
themes.example: The growth of a middle class in the Gilded Age changed ideas about leisure and family.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains why rivalry between Britain and France intensified in the mid-1700s?
choices: French settlers moved into the British colonies on the Atlantic coast and took over much of the best farmland there
The growing colonial population expanded into the interior, threatening French–Indian trade and Native autonomy
Britain wanted to end the fur trade in North America so that colonists could focus on farming
American Indian nations asked Britain to fight France so that Native peoples could trade with Spain
questions.explanation: As colonists moved west, they came into conflict with French trading networks and with Native nations who wanted to keep their lands.
choiceExplanations: French settlements were in the St. Lawrence valley and the interior, not on the British Atlantic coast.
As colonists moved west, they came into conflict with French trading networks and with Native nations who wanted to keep their lands.
The fur trade was valuable to France and to Native nations, and Britain also traded for furs.
Native nations had their own interests and did not make this request.
questions.distinguisher: The fur-trade choice is close because the fur trade was part of the conflict, but Britain did not try to end it.
questions.subskillText: Explain a historical concept, development, or process.

questions.prompt: Which region was at the center of the dispute between Britain and France that began the Seven Years' War in North America?
choices: The Ohio River Valley, which both empires claimed and many Native nations inhabited
The Great Plains west of the Mississippi River, which neither empire had explored or settled
The coast of the Carolinas, where French ships had attacked English trading posts for years
The St. Lawrence River valley, which Britain claimed and the French had never settled or governed
questions.explanation: Both Britain and France claimed the Ohio Valley, and the first fighting of the war took place there in 1754.
choiceExplanations: Both Britain and France claimed the Ohio Valley, and the first fighting of the war took place there in 1754.
Fighting began in the Ohio Valley, east of the Mississippi.
The dispute was in the interior rather than on the Carolina coast.
The St. Lawrence valley was the heart of French Canada.
questions.distinguisher: The St. Lawrence choice is close because Quebec later fell to the British, but the war began over the Ohio Valley.
questions.subskillText: Identify a historical concept, development, or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains why Britain looked to the colonies for revenue after 1763?
choices: Colonial merchants had refused to pay the customs duties that Britain collected before the war began
Britain wanted to punish the colonies for having refused to send soldiers to fight in the war
France demanded payments from Britain, and Britain asked colonists to send gold and silver to Paris
The war had left Britain deeply in debt with a larger empire to defend, and officials thought the colonies should help pay
questions.explanation: Victory brought a large new territory to defend and a large debt, so officials decided that the colonies should share the cost.
choiceExplanations: The problem after 1763 was Britain's war debt, not unpaid customs from before the war.
Colonial militias had fought in the war, and Britain's concern was its debt.
France lost the war and did not collect payments from Britain.
Victory brought a large new territory to defend and a large debt, so officials decided that the colonies should share the cost.
questions.distinguisher: The punishment choice is close because colonists later felt punished, but the cause was the cost of the war.
questions.subskillText: Explain how a historical development or process relates to another historical development or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a result of the Treaty of Paris of 1763?
choices: Britain gave Florida to France in return for Canada and its claims east of the Mississippi River
France kept Canada but gave Britain its claims in the Ohio Valley and the Great Lakes region
France gave up Canada and its claims east of the Mississippi River, and Britain gained Florida
Spain gained all of the land east of the Mississippi River in exchange for aid to Britain
questions.explanation: Britain emerged with Canada, the land east of the Mississippi, and Florida, which made its North American empire much larger.
choiceExplanations: Britain gained Florida from Spain and Canada from France.
France gave up Canada as well as its claims east of the Mississippi.
Britain emerged with Canada, the land east of the Mississippi, and Florida, which made its North American empire much larger.
Spain gave up Florida and received Louisiana from France.
questions.distinguisher: The Florida-exchange choice is close because Florida was exchanged, but it went to Britain, not to France.
questions.subskillText: Identify a historical concept, development, or process.

questions.prompt: The Proclamation of 1763 was intended to
choices: avoid new wars with Native nations by forbidding settlement west of the Appalachian Mountains
raise revenue for the Crown by selling the western lands to colonists at high prices
give colonial assemblies authority to govern and distribute the western territories as they wished
reward soldiers who had fought for Britain by granting each of them a farm in the Ohio country
questions.explanation: The Crown wanted to reduce conflict with Native nations, many of whom feared the loss of their land, by limiting settlement west of the mountains.
choiceExplanations: The Crown wanted to reduce conflict with Native nations, many of whom feared the loss of their land, by limiting settlement west of the mountains.
The proclamation closed the western lands to settlement rather than selling them.
The Crown kept control of the western lands and gave assemblies no such authority.
Settlement of the Ohio country was restricted by the proclamation.
questions.distinguisher: The revenue choice is close because Britain needed money, but the proclamation was a security measure and restricted settlement.
questions.subskillText: Explain a historical concept, development, or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains why Native nations of the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley attacked British forts in 1763?
choices: They had joined the colonists in a campaign against the Crown and its tax policies in North America
They feared the spread of British settlement and disliked British trade policies after the French defeat
They believed that the Proclamation of 1763 had opened their lands to British settlers and traders
They had been ordered by the Spanish to attack British forts so that Spain could take the Ohio Valley
questions.explanation: With the French gone, Native nations lost a trading partner and counterweight, and they feared that colonists would move onto their lands.
choiceExplanations: Taxation disputes between the colonists and Britain came later, and Native nations acted on their own concerns.
With the French gone, Native nations lost a trading partner and counterweight, and they feared that colonists would move onto their lands.
The proclamation restricted settlement, and the attacks had begun before it was issued.
Native nations acted for their own reasons, not on Spanish orders.
questions.distinguisher: The proclamation choice is close because the proclamation was linked to the war, but it followed the first attacks and was meant to limit settlement.
questions.subskillText: Explain how a historical development or process relates to another historical development or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the colonial reaction to the Proclamation of 1763?
choices: Colonists welcomed the proclamation because it protected them from Native attacks and from French rule
Colonial assemblies passed laws requiring every settler to return to the coast within one year
Many colonists, who had expected western lands, resented the restriction, and some settled there anyway
Colonists accepted the proclamation because it gave each colony a share of the western lands
questions.explanation: The line was hard to enforce, and the restriction added to colonial opposition to British policy.
choiceExplanations: Many colonists, including veterans and land speculators, wanted western land and resented the limit.
The assemblies did not order settlers back, and many settlers moved west anyway.
The line was hard to enforce, and the restriction added to colonial opposition to British policy.
The proclamation reserved the land for Native peoples and did not distribute it to colonies.
questions.distinguisher: The welcome choice is close because the proclamation did reduce the risk of conflict, but it blocked expectations of land.
questions.subskillText: Explain how a historical development or process relates to another historical development or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the Albany Plan of Union of 1754?
choices: Britain created a union of the colonies under a royal governor to fight the French in the Ohio Valley
The colonies formed a permanent government that taxed the colonists to pay for the war with France
The colonies signed a treaty with the Iroquois to join the French against the British
Colonial delegates considered a plan for a union of the colonies, but no colony approved it
questions.explanation: Benjamin Franklin and other delegates proposed a union at Albany, but the colonial assemblies were unwilling to give up power.
choiceExplanations: The Albany Plan was proposed by colonists, and Britain did not impose it.
The colonies did not form a permanent government.
The colonies hoped to keep the Iroquois as allies against the French.
Benjamin Franklin and other delegates proposed a union at Albany, but the colonial assemblies were unwilling to give up power.
questions.distinguisher: The royal-governor choice is close because Britain did later direct the war, but the Albany Plan came from the colonies.
questions.subskillText: Identify a historical concept, development, or process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
choices: France won the war but lost control of its colonies because of the Proclamation of 1763
Britain's victory brought new territory but also debt and duties that shaped its colonial policies
The colonists defeated the French by themselves and expected Britain to reward them with western land
American Indians gained control of the Appalachian Mountains as a result of the Treaty of Paris
questions.explanation: The passage describes the territory Britain gained, the debt it carried, and the policies that followed, including the Proclamation of 1763.
choiceExplanations: The passage says Britain won the war and that France gave up Canada.
The passage describes the territory Britain gained, the debt it carried, and the policies that followed, including the Proclamation of 1763.
The passage describes a British victory and does not credit the colonists alone.
The passage describes the Proclamation of 1763, not a transfer of control to Native nations.
questions.distinguisher: The colonist choice is close because the passage mentions that colonists expected western lands, but it does not say they won the war alone.

stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing how historians describe the results of the Seven Years' War in North America
stimulusBlocks.text:
The Seven Years' War ended in 1763 with a great British victory. In the Treaty of Paris, France gave up Canada and its claims east of the Mississippi River, and Spain gave Florida to Britain. The victory removed the French threat to the colonies, but it left Britain deeply in debt and responsible for a much larger empire.

British officials decided that the colonies should help pay for their own defense. They also wanted to avoid new wars with American Indians, many of whom had fought beside the French and now feared the loss of their land. In the Proclamation of 1763, the Crown forbade colonists from settling west of the Appalachian Mountains. Many colonists, who had expected to move onto western lands after the war, resented the order, and many ignored it.

questions.subskillText: Identify and describe a claim and/or argument in a text-based or non-text-based source.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Crown forbid colonists from settling west of the Appalachian Mountains?
choices: Officials wanted to avoid new wars with American Indians who feared the loss of their land
Officials wanted to keep the colonists close to the coast where they could be taxed more easily
Officials wanted to hold the western lands for the French, who had been promised them by treaty
Officials wanted to prevent colonists from fighting other colonists over control of the western lands
questions.explanation: The passage states that British officials wished to avoid new wars with American Indians, who now feared the loss of their land.
choiceExplanations: The passage states that British officials wished to avoid new wars with American Indians, who now feared the loss of their land.
The passage links the order to the danger of new wars with American Indians.
The passage says France gave up its claims east of the Mississippi.
The passage does not mention disputes among colonists as the reason.
questions.distinguisher: The taxation choice is close because the passage says colonists should pay for defense, but it gives a different reason for the Proclamation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following details from the passage best supports the claim that Britain's victory created new problems for the empire?
choices: France gave up Canada and its claims east of the Mississippi River in the Treaty of Paris
Spain gave Florida to Britain at the end of the war in the Treaty of Paris
The victory removed the French threat to the colonies after the end of the war
The victory left Britain deeply in debt and responsible for a much larger empire
questions.explanation: The debt and the larger empire were the costs of victory, and they pushed Britain toward new policies for the colonies.
choiceExplanations: This detail describes a gain for Britain and not a problem.
This detail describes a territorial gain for Britain.
This detail describes a benefit of the victory.
The debt and the larger empire were the costs of victory, and they pushed Britain toward new policies for the colonies.
questions.distinguisher: The French-threat choice is close because it comes from the same sentence, but it describes a benefit, not a problem.
